ANL/ESIA-25/2 Vol. 3 Application of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) Systems for Powering Safety Monitoring Systems of Offshore Oil and Gas Operations OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report: Collocation of OTEC with Offshore Oil and Gas Activities Energy Systems and Infrastructure Analysis Division Acknowledgments This study was funded by the Offshore Energy Safety Institute (OESI) 2.0 managed by the Texas A&M University Engineering Experiment Station (TEES). The funding award was made under OESI 2.0 R&D track entitled “M-T1-P1.1 Mapping use cases and connecting small- scale marine energy solutions to enhance the safety, security, and sustainability of oil & gas operations.” The authors wish to express gratitude to the members of the OESI 2.0 Steering Committee for their input and guidance. Special thanks to Kalyan Raj Kota, Evan Zimmerman, Faisal Khan, Michael Eldred, Nina Joffe, Sebastian Grimm, Carrie Shamus, and Jay Parle for their invaluable advice and insights. Additionally, this study relied upon input from academia, government, and offshore oil and gas industry experts, who generously donated their time to share with the authors the relevant details of certain equipment types and approaches described in this study. The authors are grateful for the time and input of Stuart Cohen and Brian Mirletz of NREL for their advice on LCOE calculations; Pak Leung and Luz Zarate of Shell for insights on the value of renewables research for offshore; Jake Keel of Baker Hughes, Andres Chavarria of Luna Innovations, and Judson Jevon of Saab Inc. for insights on well monitoring solutions; Ram Seetharam and Brian Gibbs of U of H ROICE Project; Cholena Ren, Holli Wecht, and Mary Rogener-Dewitt of BOEM for insights on ongoing research and development efforts; and Sudhakar Tallavajhula of Technip and Luiz Feijo of ABS for insights on physical limitations of floating facilities related to potential OTEC coupling.
